[BugFix][Quantization] Fail fast on MXFP checkpoints for devices without an MX matmul (#21893)

Refs #21604

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MXFP-quantized ModelSlim **weight** checkpoints (`W8A8_MXFP8`,
`W4A8_MXFP`,
`W4A4_MXFP4`, `W4A16_MXFP4`) always quantize with the A5 MX kernel, so
they can
only execute on Ascend 950. On A2/A3 the failure used to surface deep
inside
weight loading as an obscure aclnn error (aclnnNpuFormatCast 161002)
after the
whole checkpoint had been read, leaving no hint that the device cannot
run the
checkpoint as published.

This PR rejects such checkpoints at scheme construction: a shared
`require_mx_weight_format(WeightFormat)` helper in `methods/base.py`,
called from
every MXFP weight-scheme `__init__`, raises `NotImplementedError` with
the
quant-format name and actionable remediation (re-quantize with
ModelSlim, e.g.
`W8A8_DYNAMIC`, or deploy on Ascend 950).

This extends the principle of #21604 (native block-wise FP8 checkpoints
are
rejected on non-950 devices) to the sibling ModelSlim path, which
`fp8_block`
never sees. The op-level runtime guards in `device_op.py` ("MXFP MoE
quantization
is only supported on Ascend A5.") stay untouched as the last line of
defense, so
the two layers form defense in depth rather than duplicate checks.

Scope notes, stated up front:

1. The C8-MXFP KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`) is deliberately
**not** gated
in `kv_cache/mxfp_c8.py`. `AscendC8MXFPKVCacheAttentionMethod` is only
   constructed when that dtype is set (`modelslim_config.py`,
`enable_mxfp_c8_quant`), and the KV-cache path already rejects
unsupported
cache dtypes (`attention_v1.py`, `kv_cache_dtype_str_to_dtype`), so a
gate
inside the method would duplicate an existing check.
`kv_cache/mxfp_c8.py` is
   unchanged in this PR.
2. A checkpoint declaring MXFP quant types is rejected as a whole;
partial
fallback is not attempted, consistent with #21604's approach for native
FP8.

An e2e negative test was not added because the e2e harness requires real
950
hardware for MXFP scheme registration; the scheme-level UT covers the
rejection
path. (For context, the mxfp_compat compatibility shim was removed by
#13447;
the current main tree has no mxfp_compat module or `ensure_mxfp*`
helpers.)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Loading a ModelSlim MXFP checkpoint on Ascend A2/A3 or Atlas 300I
DUO now
fails at model construction with an actionable message, instead of
failing
minutes later inside weight loading with an opaque aclnnNpuFormatCast
error.

### How was this patch tested?

- `pytest tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_mx_weight_format_gate.py` —
21 new
unit tests: the helper's reject/pass branches for both MXFP8 and MXFP4,
one
reject/pass case per MXFP weight-scheme family (W8A8 linear/MoE, the
DeepSeek
sparse variant, W4A8, W4A4, the FlatQuant variant, W4A16), and a
non-MXFP
scheme proving it stays unguarded. The hardware profile is mocked so
both
  branches run on any machine.
- Existing tests that construct MXFP schemes were updated to pin a
profile with
MXFP8 support, same as #21604 did for `test_fp8_block.py`. A
pristine-main vs
patched regression run over the affected quantization/model tests shows
zero
  new failures.
- Real-device (A3) probe: the real hardware profile resolves MXFP8/MXFP4
support
as False and constructing the `W8A8_MXFP8` linear scheme raises the
actionable
  `NotImplementedError`, while `W8A8_DYNAMIC` constructs unaffected.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: both gate branches
(reject/pass) covered
per scheme family; non-MXFP scheme covered as the unaffected control
group.
- [x] **Regression test**: scheme-construction tests now fail without
the gate
mocks; the gate itself fails closed on hardware without MX support.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the reject branch of every
gated scheme is
      asserted, including exception type and message content.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the mocked-profile pattern
matches the one
      #21604 introduced for `test_fp8_block.py`.

[Feature][KV Pool] Reuse GVA layerwise transfer for DS4.1 shared KV (#21949)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 stores shared KV only at selected source layers. Use the
existing GVA layerwise worker, task queues, and lifecycle. There is no
new cross-layer transfer mode or worker.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DS4.1 can use Memcache GVA layerwise pooling via the existing
`backend: "memcache"` and `use_layerwise: true` settings, including
composite Mooncake V2 push with MultiConnector. No new environment
variable or transfer-mode setting is added.

This path requires Model Runner V2 and eager execution
(`--enforce-eager`). TP/PCP are supported; PP/DCP/KVPP and graph replay
remain outside the supported scope. No additional startup guards are
introduced for those unsupported configurations.

[BugFix] Exclude host driver install info from Ascend C cache identity (#20737)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Remove the single `/etc/ascend_install.info` entry from
`_candidate_cann_metadata_files()`.

This file records the host driver installation and can be mounted only
when a container starts. Including it in `compiler_environment_hash` can
invalidate the cache produced while building the same image, even though
the operator compiler environment has not changed.

The patch is limited to **one file and one deleted line**. The other
cache inputs and all three hash algorithms retain their existing
behavior.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Build-cache reuse no longer depends on the runtime-mounted host driver
installation record.

The reporter has verified this minimal fix.

[BugFix][Test] Declare GDN batch-invariance support and cover Qwen3.5-35B-A3B in the TP4 e2e (#19442)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The TP4 batch-invariance e2e only covered `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B`: all full
attention, MoE routing at 128 experts with no shared expert.
`Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` is a hybrid MoE whose 40 layers repeat a 3:1
pattern, so 30 are gated-delta-net linear-attention layers and 10 are
full attention, and every layer runs the Qwen3-Next style MoE block with
256 experts, top-8 and one shared expert. MoE routing was therefore
already covered; the GDN layers, the linear/full interleave and that MoE
block were not, even though
`docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/batch_invariance.md` already lists
the model as supported on A3.

This PR:

- declares batch-invariance support on the Ascend GDN backend
(`AscendGDNAttentionBackend.supports_batch_invariance()`), without which
the new case cannot even start: vLLM #60271 checks every layer's backend
in `init_attn_backend`, Qwen3.5's GDN layers assign the Ascend backend
directly (`patch_qwen3_5` replaces `get_attn_backend`, so the selector's
own check never sees them), and the engine aborted with `RuntimeError:
VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for GDN_ATTN.` The GDN family
is also added to `tests/ut/attention/test_batch_invariance_support.py`,
so dropping the declaration again fails a CPU UT;
- moves the BS=1 vs BS=N comparison into
`_assert_bitwise_batch_invariance()` and folds the shared engine kwargs
into `_model()`, so both models share one body and one configuration: a
new model is a marker block plus a one-line wrapper;
- splits the batch-invariance e2e by model family: the Qwen cases live
in `rlhf/consistency/batch_invariant/test_qwen.py`, the shared BS=1 vs
BS=N comparison and the batch-invariant env in
`tests/e2e/common/rlhf/batch_invariant/common.py` (parallel to
`common/rlhf/weight_transfer`), so a new family is one file instead of
growing a single file;
- adds the Qwen3.5 case on the real 40-layer checkpoint with the same
defaults as the Qwen3 case (`max_num_seqs=144`, `max_model_len=8192`,
TP4, bf16, no prefix caching, `cudagraph_capture_sizes=[1, 32, 64]`,
`graph_mode="full_and_piecewise"`). Its `gpu_memory_utilization` is 0.9,
env-overridable; that is the value it was measured with at TP4. No
layer-reduced slice and no per-case memory cap: with ten full-attention
layers the per-layer fused-attention workspace is the KV cache divided
by ten, so the slice's "cache twice" constraint does not apply;
- keeps the original `pytest.skip` when `RequestOutput` carries no
logprobs, and does not add assertions on the served config;
- fixes the existing case's `e2e_coverage(hardware=...)`: it claimed
`A2`, but `four_card` tests route to `a3-4`, and every other `four_card`
case says `A3`.

No release-note fragment: this is a bugfix, not a user-facing feature.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, in behaviour: `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` can start and run with
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on Ascend again; before this PR the engine
refused to start because the GDN backend did not declare batch-invariant
support. No API or configuration change.

### How was this patch tested?

CI on the four-card A3 runner, one pytest process for the whole file:

```bash
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4
python -m pytest tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/rlhf/consistency/batch_invariant/test_qwen.py -sv
```

The full-40-layer version of this case already ran green on both vLLM
lanes (`2 passed` per lane, ~6 min each): token ids and the float32
logprobs of the sampled tokens are bitwise equal for 32 prompts between
BS=1 and one BS=32 batch. The current revision only moves the shared
kwargs into `_model()` and drops the per-case assertions, so it is the
same engine configuration; CI on this head is the confirmation.

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: not applicable, the case

[Test] Focus PD combination coverage on the V2 pull Scheduler regression (#19610)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds a real-`Scheduler` regression for the V2 Mooncake pull connector
(`MooncakeConnectorV2`) under PD disaggregation with speculative
decoding, as requested in #10654. Part of the external contributor task
pool #9079.

The producer scheduler truncates the last prompt token **before** the
local prefix-cache lookup — for every speculative configuration
(disabled / MTP / DSpark) — so prefix-cache hit counts stay consistent
with the scheduled prompt. The regression drives the real `Scheduler`
(`add_request` → `schedule` → `update_from_output`) with mocked
transport only: the worker handshake thread is stubbed and remote
completion is injected through `KVConnectorOutput`.

Reworked per the review of the initial revision:

- Rebased onto current main; the V2 pull Scheduler regression is now the
single focus of this PR, placed under
`tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/`.
- Kept the boundary cases that exercise the real `Scheduler`: prompt
lengths 512/513/514 around the truncation boundary (warm / hit / shorter
/ longer runs), each ending with `assert_scheduler_empty`.
- The `Scheduler` construction mutates process-global state; the test
now snapshots and restores the KVCacheSpec registry
(`vllm.v1.kv_cache_spec_registry`) and the prefix-cache hash state
(`NONE_HASH` / `_NONE_HASH_SEED`) after the run, so later tests observe
the pristine state.
- Dropped from the first revision: the legacy connector additions, the
KVPP e2e cases, and the reviewer notes tied to them (the e2e directory
layout note and the cross-file `sys.modules` pollution finding — happy
to report the pollution one separately if maintainers prefer). A
topology / rank-mapping follow-up for supported V2 pull/push
configurations will be sent separately.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Tests only.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests, CPU-mock mode (CI-isomorphic): vllm at the current verified
main commit `24420b7a3`, vllm-ascend on this branch rebased onto main
`d476b0097`.

- New file alone: 3 passed (spec-decode disabled / MTP / DSpark).

[BugFix][Attention] Rebind FIA workspace query in batch invariant mode (#21176)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`enable_batch_invariant_mode()` swaps
`torch_npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score` for the
batch-invariant packet, but leaves
`torch_npu._npu_fused_infer_attention_score_get_max_workspace`
pointing at the non-batch-invariant helper. `full_graph_fia()` in
`vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py` sizes the FIA workspace with
that helper and then
registers the task for the batch-invariant kernel, so the two disagree
about the workspace
size.

On Ascend 950 the disagreement is fatal at capture time:

```
call aclnnFusedInferAttentionScoreBatchInvariantV5 failed,
detail: Invalid_Argument(EZ1010):
Value 203456512 for parameter workspaceSize is invalid.
Reason: The passed workspace size 203456512 does not meet the minimum workspace size
487327744 actually required by the AutoContiguous API.
```

194 MiB is allocated for a kernel that needs 465 MiB. It surfaces as
`capture_end ... error code is 107033 ... task group status error`,
which points away from
the real cause: the operator failed inside the graph task group, so
nobody calls
`graph_task_group_end` and `rtStreamEndCapture` reports an unfinished
group. The same model
and configuration with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` captures 4/4, which
shows the graph path is
fine and only the two `torch_npu` symbols are out of sync.

This PR binds the workspace query to the batch-invariant counterpart
when the installed
`batch_invariant_ops` exposes it. If the installed package has no such
symbol, it binds a
stub that raises on first use, so full graph capture can never silently
size the workspace
with the non-BI query. Eager and PIECEWISE are unaffected, because they
never call it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: batch invariant mode combined with ACL graph capture now works on
A3 and Ascend 950
instead of failing during graph capture. No new API, config key or
environment variable is
added.

### How was this patch tested?

Hardware: Ascend 950DT (8 die), CANN 9.2.1, torch 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu
2.10.0.post7,
vLLM `ced6857`, vllm-ascend `c09d3e20b`, `batch_invariant_ops` 2.0.0.
Model: Qwen3-30B-A3B (48 layers, 32 Q / 4 KV, head_dim 128, bf16), TP=1,
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `HCCL_DETERMINISTIC=strict`,
`enforce_eager=False`
(`cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, capture sizes 1/2/4/8), chunked
prefill and prefix
caching disabled, block size 128.

- before the fix: FULL capture fails on the first bucket with the EZ1010
above; PIECEWISE
  captures 4/4
- after the fix: PIECEWISE 4/4 + FULL 4/4, `fia_graph_calls=192` (48
layers x 4 buckets),
`fia_forward_capturing=192`, no eager FIA call during decode
(`fia_eager_calls=2112` is
  prefill only), `pa_calls=0`, 1240 graph replays
- batch invariance, bitwise (`torch.equal` on token ids, chosen logprob
compared via
`float.hex`, top-5 logprob the same way): repeat 0/2, BS=2/3/4/8 all 0
mismatches, needle
0/24; the same numbers hold in eager mode, and two independent graph
runs are bitwise
  identical
- at runtime the FIA packet is the batch-invariant one and both the
`default` and the `out`
overload report `is_bi=true`; the graph path goes through `out`, so the
captured kernel is
  the BI one

A3 (16 die, `ascend910_9382`), CANN 9.2.0, torch 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu
2.10.0.post7,
vLLM `24420b7a`, vllm-ascend main, `batch_invariant_ops` built for A3.
Same model, TP=4,
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `enforce_eager=False`
(`cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, capture
sizes 1/2/4/8/16), `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`. The gap is wider than
on Ascend 950:

- before the fix: `EZ1010 ... Value 235274240 for parameter
workspaceSize is invalid ...
does not meet the minimum workspace size 820904960`, on all 4 ranks,
capture 0/4
- after the fix: capture 4/4, `full_graph_fia=240` (48 layers x 5
buckets), no EZ1010
- CANN 9.3.0 fails the same way with a slightly different requirement
(820773888) and is
fixed the same way; on CANN 9.1.0 the two queries do not cross the
limit, so capture
  already succeeded there without the change

Scope note on the hardware evidence: the measurement above used an
application-level rebind
of the same two symbols (`import batch_invariant_ops as bops;
torch_npu._npu_fused_infer_attention_score_get_max_workspace =
bops._npu_...`), applied
before engine construction, on both Ascend 950 and A3. This exact commit
has not been
re-run on the device; the code here is those same two assignments moved
into
`enable_batch_invariant_mode()`. Raw logs and
the JSON result files can be attached on request.

Unit tests: two cases in `tests/ut/test_batch_invariant.py` cover the
rebind and the fallback
for builds without the symbol. They were checked locally with `ruff
check` / `ruff format`
v0.14.0 (the version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`); the NPU unit
test runs in CI.

Note: this makes batch invariant + full graph work for FIA (GQA) models.
MLA / SFA attention
still needs its own batch-invariant kernel coverage, tracked in #5487.

`batch_invariant_ops` has no workspace query symbol, and a unit test

- [x] **Regression test**:
`test_enable_batch_invariant_mode_rebinds_fia_workspace_query`

- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the fallback path (symbol
missing) is covered.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the tests assert the rebound

[CI][Misc] Modify cudagraph_mode for step3p7 nightly (#22100)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Setting `cudagraph_mode` to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` causes a clear prefill
regression for long inputs. For step3p7 the prefill chunk is on the
order of 16k tokens, far above the cudagraph capture limit (288), so
prefill is never replayed from a captured graph in either mode.
`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` nonetheless splits the compiled prefill graph at
attention boundaries (20+ splitting points) and forcibly disables
`enable_npugraph_ex`, paying per-segment dispatch and synchronization
overhead while gaining none of the benefits of piecewise execution
(which only helps small mixed prefill+decode batches). This PR switches
the default to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: prefill is no longer split,
`enable_npugraph_ex` stays enabled, and decode remains covered by the
FULL graph.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No.
### How was this patch tested?
CI and Nightly tests.

[Refactor][KV Cache] Let MLA and indexer owners publish final MRV2 cache specs (#21370)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MRV2 currently derives MLA and indexer cache storage formats in the
collector, duplicating information owned by the attention layer and its
backend. This PR moves spec construction to those owners so the
collector receives the final storage format.

- `AscendMLAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec()` preserves upstream metadata,
selects the FA/SFA C8 or TurboQuant format, and reuses the
implementation's packed KV width.
- `AscendSFAIndexerCache` publishes its backend-built spec, including
scale storage and context-parallel replication, while preserving the
disabled-preprocessing and MTP cases.
- The collector applies upstream `customize_attention_spec` to attention
specs, including kernel-block alignment, and retains HiSparse handling.

[Performance] Pin shared KV mmap and parallelize startup population (#21101)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Native KV tiering uses pageable shared memory and repeats full-region
pre-faulting on replicated MLA workers. Support opt-in pinning of the
existing mapping for direct batched transfers, and distribute worker
pre-faulting across the shared region.

- When pinning is enabled, register each worker's slots for
non-replicated layouts; replicated MLA workers register the complete
shared mapping.
- Reuse upstream's segment count and
`populate_shard=(logical_worker_rank, world_size)` where available.
MLA's data-slot rank remains zero.
- Construct scheduler and worker mappings with identical segment
parameters. Reuse upstream primary/secondary/tiering managers; override
their construction because upstream `get_manager` hardcodes a
single-file region.
- Run `_all_workers_barrier` after worker population, before host
pinning. EngineCore initializes workers before the scheduler: passing
this barrier into the CPU region constructor would unlink files before
the scheduler could attach. Keep backing paths during successful
startup; detach creator-owned names when initialization aborts or during
shutdown.
- Roll back failed registrations, synchronize before unregistering, and
preserve registered views if release fails. Population failure releases
peers; barrier and scheduler-construction failures clean up constructed
resources.

- Keep each shared mapping and its registered tensor views in a
process-scoped registration owner until unregister succeeds. If
construction/rollback fails and the unfinished worker is
garbage-collected, the mapping remains owned until recovery or process
exit. A lock protects registry membership only; synchronization and ACL
calls run outside it.

- Detach creator-owned backing names independently of unmapping when
initialization aborts or shutdown starts. Even failed handler
cleanup/synchronization/unregister cannot skip this unlink step.
Registered mappings remain owned and usable; non-creators leave the
creator files intact. Handle every backing segment and older single-file
mappings.

Uses the existing C++ bindings. No environment variable or
registration-scope configuration was added. Based on upstream main
`9005a22a862a95d52025b70fb2bff8eed8a5a5e3`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `TieringOffloadingSpec` supports opt-in shared-mmap pinning on
supported builds and uses parallel population on supported vLLM
versions.

- `pin_shared_mmap` defaults to `false`; set it to `true` to enable host
registration.
- Registration scope follows the cache layout automatically.
- Handle both the older `_REGION_SEGMENTS` and newer `REGION_SEGMENTS`
upstream names.
- `CPUOffloadingSpec` retains its pinned tensor allocator.

Release note: `release_notes/fragments/21101.yaml`.

Usage: [CPU offload
guide](https://github.com/ckeyever/vllm-ascend/blob/79749e52b7bb2e0d198ae5dbd007206ca91203af/docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_cpu_offload.md#pinning-the-shared-cpu-tier)
documents `pin_shared_mmap` placement, its default, an enable example,
automatic registration scope, fallback behavior and population-time
scaling.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Pinning performance comparison

User-reported pinning enabled/disabled measurements; not independently
rerun on the final PR. These results concern pinning and do not measure
sharded-population startup time.

| Model | Mean TTFT without pin (ms) | Mean TTFT with pin (ms) | Mean
TTFT reduction | Per-byte DMA without pin (GB/s) | Per-byte DMA with pin
(GB/s) | Per-byte DMA improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-1.7B | 41,284 | 30,114 | 27.06% | 8.23 | 13.27 | +61.24% |
| GLM-5.2 | 209,937 | 195,638 | 6.81% | 1.94 | 2.49 | +28.35% |

Both percentages use the non-pinned result as the baseline:

- Mean TTFT reduction = (TTFT without pin - TTFT with pin) / TTFT
without pin x 100%.
- Per-byte DMA improvement = (DMA with pin - DMA without pin) / DMA
without pin x 100%.

Local CPU validation:

explicitly disabled and explicitly enabled pinning; existing failure
regressions explicitly enable registration. Synchronization/unregister
failure intentionally skips mmap cleanup so the registration owner keeps

[Feature] Support prefill KVPP in Mooncake Push (#21805)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable prefill-side KVPP with `MooncakePushConnector` for supported
non-hybrid MLA/SFA models, including GLM-5.3 W8A8C8. Push previously
chose a producer replica by destination rank. With KVPP, that rank can
lack the layer's persistent cache, leaving a decode worker with missing
data even after all producer ranks report DONE.

Reuse the owner map from cache registration. A target layer's persistent
owner writes that layer to each decode worker that has it. Replicated
MTP caches still select one producer per destination. Decode keeps KVPP
disabled.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Set `"enable_kvpp": true` on the prefill node when both nodes use
`MooncakePushConnector`. Decode leaves KVPP disabled. Prefill uses DCP=1
when KVPP is enabled. Decode can use the existing Push DCP path with
compatible cache layouts.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Local CPU/mock** — Used the workspace's existing
`vllm-ascend/.venv`, the base branch's pinned vLLM source
(`24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58`), and a temporary dependency
overlay for Transformers 5.20.2, huggingface-hub 1.33.0 and tokenizers
0.23.3. The default environment failed collection due to a Transformers
mismatch. With the overlay, `uv run --active pytest -q
tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2 tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py -k
'mooncake_v2 or KVPP'` reported **681 passed, 159 deselected, 27
subtests passed**.
- **A3 host (.5), Mooncake V2 unit suite** — `python3 -m pytest -q
--noconftest tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2` reported **675 passed** on
the clean PR tree. The new regression uses P TP2 × PCP2 and D TP2. It
checks bytes and exactly one write per destination cache component for
every required target layer, LI C8 keys and scales, and the selected MTP
replica.
- **A3 host (.5), real Mooncake NPU WRITE** — Mooncake Transfer Engine
0.3.13, Ascend Direct, four NPUs with P TP2 / D TP2, and KVPP enabled
only on P. Allocated synthetic pages using the non-Flash GLM-5.3 cache
dimensions and seeded distinct patterns per P rank and layer. Ran real
cache registration, D metadata discovery, layerwise WRITE and DONE
through the Push workers. Both D ranks received all producer DONEs and
matched the expected bytes for two packed SFA C8 target layers, LI C8
keys and scales, and one MTP layer. Adjacent blocks kept their sentinel
values. Full-model serving was outside this smoke test.
- **Single-node DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat end-to-end test on A3 (.5).**
Loaded the full BF16 checkpoint with vLLM 0.33.0 and Model Runner V2 in
eager mode. Ran Prefill with TP2 and Decode with TP1 on three NPUs on
the same host, using the layerwise proxy and `MooncakePushConnector`.
Decode kept KVPP disabled. Compared Prefill KVPP on and off with three
greedy requests of 5, 563, and 527 input tokens, each generating 24
tokens. All three completion texts matched exactly. The two longer
prompts exercised chunked prefill with a 256-token batch limit. With
KVPP enabled, the two Prefill ranks advertised 14 and 13 persistent
cache layers, and Decode registered all 27 layers.

[CI] Add slipcover for UT coverage checking (#20583)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds an incremental UT coverage gate and PR-comment coverage reporting
to the CI pipeline, and fixes 17 test cases that fail under parallel
`pytest-xdist` execution.

- Fixes: #20581 

Two commits:

- `[CI] Add slipcover for UT coverage checking` (`cdccf7e12`) —
slipcover + pytest-xdist + diff-cover collection, an 80% new-line
coverage gate on `cpu-ut`, and a single coverage-comment poster that
also works for fork PRs (`.github/workflows`, +238/-2).
- `[CI] Fix parallel test UT case failures` (`70d47e0e1`) — hardens
tests that depend on worker-local state, fixed ports, or tight timing
against parallel xdist scheduling (17 files, +210/-44).

**Coverage collection (slipcover + pytest-xdist, cpu only)**

- Installs `slipcover>=1.0.18`, `pytest-xdist`, and `diff-cover` in the
cpu-ut environment (`.github/workflows/_selected_tests.yaml`).
- Replaces the plain `pytest -sv` in the default UT path
(`.github/workflows/scripts/run_selected_tests.sh`, both single-target
and batch modes) with:
  ```bash
  python -m slipcover --source="${project_root}/vllm_ascend" \
--omit="*/tests/*" --json --out "${project_root}/tests/coverage.json" \
    -m pytest -n auto -sv --color=yes <targets...>
  ```
- slipcover: near-zero-overhead measurement (~5% vs ~180% median for
traditional coverage.py);
- `-n auto`: parallel execution across the runner's CPU cores; slipcover
(≥1.0.18) automatically merges coverage data from all xdist workers;
- the CLI rejects `--json` and `--xml` together, so the run emits JSON
only, and a follow-up step converts it to Cobertura XML (`python -m
slipcover --merge ./tests/coverage.json --xml --out
./tests/coverage.xml`).
- NPU targets keep plain `pytest` — on NPU runners each xdist worker
initializes torch_npu plus an engine subprocess, which crashed the
shared runner (run 111649013424: 22/22 e2e jobs failed with no
test-level errors) and contended for card memory (17/24 e2e jobs
failed). NPU e2e targets run serially; cpu keeps `-n auto`. The coverage
steps are guarded by `matrix.group.npu_type == 'cpu'` because NPU jobs
never produce `coverage.json`.

**Incremental coverage gate (diff-cover)**

After the test run, the reusable workflow runs `diff-cover` twice:

1. without a threshold, generating `tests/diff_coverage.md` — the report
always exists and is uploaded (`if: !cancelled()`), so the comment is
posted even when coverage is below the threshold;
2. with `--fail-under=80` against `origin/${{ github.base_ref }}` —
enforcing the gate separately so below-threshold coverage still fails
the job (and therefore `ci-gate`).

**Coverage report presentation (PR comment, fork-safe)**

- The markdown report is uploaded as the `coverage-report` artifact
(`if: !cancelled()`).
- A fork PR's `pull_request` GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only, so all comment
posting lives in the new `post_fork_coverage_comment.yaml` with
`pull-requests: write`:
- `workflow_run` (E2E completed) is the main trigger — it fires on any
completed run, green or not, so a failing coverage gate still gets its
report commented;
- `pull_request_target` (opened/synchronize) covers runs that finished
before the PR was opened;
- the PR number for forks travels via the `pr-context` artifact (new
`upload-pr-context` job in `pr_test.yaml`, `if: !cancelled()`) because
`workflow_run` payloads carry an empty `pull_requests[]` for fork PRs;
- security: the workflow never checks out or executes the fork's code —
it only downloads artifacts from the trusted `pr_test.yaml` run;
`comment_tag` keeps updating the same comment.
- Both workflows run on `linux-amd64-cpu-8-hk`: this org has no
GitHub-hosted runners, so `ubuntu-latest` would queue forever.
- Known limitation: `workflow_run`-triggered workflows run the default
branch's copy of the file, so that path activates after merge; during
the PR lifetime the `pull_request_target` path covers it.

**Parallel-UT hardening (17 files, fixes grouped by root cause)**

Today's UT only verifies pass/fail — a PR can merge new code with zero
test coverage. Running the cpu suite in parallel (`-n auto`) then
surfaced pre-existing worker-local state, fixed ports, and tight timing
assumptions:

1. **xdist worker global state**: snapshot/restore `_ASCEND_CONFIG` in
`test_linear` (a MagicMock leak broke 22 downstream cases via
`FileExistsError`); re-`importlib.reload` the platform module after the
patched reload in `test_platform` (by-value imports stay rebound to
mocks); register built-in KV-cache specs first in
`test_glm5next_kv_cache`; pin the uninitialized-config branch in
`test_moe_mlp`; mock `get_current_vllm_config` in `test_mla_v1` like the
sibling test class.
2. **Fixed-port collisions**: per-worker `MASTER_PORT` offsets in 4 e2e
compile tests (`EADDRINUSE`), per-worker port offsets in
`test_load_balance_proxy_server` (`PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` gwN, 100-port
step).
3. **Timing**: relaxed subprocess/thread budgets
(`test_build_cache_concurrency`, `test_mooncake_hybrid`, rfork
session-server seed timeout 3s→30s incl. an EBADF mid-startup case); a
gate latch in `test_bus_worker` for determinism; tolerance for the lazy
`status_counter` assignment window in
`tools/profiling/aisbench_request_marker.py`.
4. **Upstream churn and numerics**: `enable_pcp` → `is_pcp_enabled`
(#19334) in `test_deepseek_v41_dspark`, `enable_dcp` → `is_dcp_enabled`
in `test_mla_v1`, and 2e-3 rtol/atol for the kimi dflash rope-cache
comparison in `test_patch_speculative_config_dflash` (CI fp32 kernels
drift by a couple of ulps; a semantic divergence such as a wrong mscale
moves values ~30% and still fails comfortably).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. CI/workflow and test-only changes; no API, interface, or runtime
behavior change for vllm-ascend users. No release note fragment.

### How was this patch tested?

- **cpu-ut + E2E CI**: 11 rounds on the branch during development
(cpu-ut matrix: vLLM main commit and release tag). The failures observed
in those runs are exactly the ones fixed by the 17-file commit — e.g.
`EADDRINUSE` port collisions in the e2e compile tests, the
`FileExistsError` cascade from the `_ASCEND_CONFIG` MagicMock leak
(cpu-ut 1031-9), and the xdist worker-crash storms on NPU runners (run
111649013424).
- **Coverage format fix**: the `--json`/`--xml` mutual exclusion was
reproduced in CI, then fixed by splitting into a JSON-only run plus a
`slipcover --merge` XML conversion.
- **Incremental gate**: verified that below-threshold coverage fails the
job (and `ci-gate`) while the report artifact is still uploaded (`if:
!cancelled()`) and the comment is still posted (the poster fires on any
completed run).
- **PR comment posting**: verified for same-repo PRs and fork PRs — the
fork chain was exercised end-to-end via the `pr-context` artifact
bridge, without ever executing fork code.
- **Existing coverage path untouched**: the `enable-coverage` + OBS
upload loop is not modified by this PR; slipcover only replaces the
default (else-branch) pytest invocation.

# [BugFix] fix sleep mode bug of deepseekv4.1

## What this PR does / why we need it?

With --engram-config {"cpu_offload": true} the DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram
tables live in registered host memory and the gather kernel reads them
over UVA. vLLM's layerwise reload — the path a checkpoint reload and
every RL weight update finish through (finalize_layerwise_reload) —
parks a layer's tensors on the meta device and materializes them again
on the device. For an offloaded table that is a full per-rank device
allocation: 22.89 GiB for a 384M x 256 BF16 table over 8 ranks (183 GiB
per table at the released size). It cannot fit next to the weights a
level-2 sleep keeps resident, so both paths die with
torch.OutOfMemoryError.

This PR makes the reload host-offload aware and adds the E2E lane that
exercises it.

#### 1. Host-offload aware layerwise reload —
`vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_offload_reload.py` (new)

The reload's call site resolves the helper through the `layerwise`
module
(`layerwise.materialize_layer`), so rebinding only
`meta.materialize_layer` would leave
the upstream implementation in place. Both names are rebound, together
with
`layerwise._copy_and_restore_kernel_tensors`:

* a parameter that carries a host range is rebuilt **on that range**,
not with
  `torch.empty_strided` on the device;
* the range is left in place instead of being copied back out of a
device copy, so an
  update written into the table is the update the lookup kernel reads;
* parameters without a host range take the upstream path unchanged.

Both hooks are upstream internals, so `install()` is defensive: a vLLM
without
`model_loader.reload`, or a release without these helpers, keeps
upstream behaviour and
logs one warning instead of failing worker startup. Registered from
`patch/worker/__init__.py`, documented in `patch/__init__.py`.

#### 2. Producer side of the attribute contract — `engram/embedding.py`

`HOST_OFFLOAD_STORAGE_ATTR` / `register_host_offload_storage()` attach
the host range a
`cpu_offload` table aliases (`_codes_uva` for `weight`, `_scales_uva`
for
`weight_scale_inv`) to the parameters. A tensor attribute survives the
meta round trip —
`to_meta_tensor` / `materialize_meta_tensor` copy `__dict__` — which is
what lets the
patched reload rebuild on host storage. A non-persistent buffer is
deliberately *not*
used here: a buffer that aliases a parameter's storage is not captured
for reloading.

#### 3. UVA address tables must survive sleep — `engram/npu.py`

`HostUvaBuffer` / `SharedUvaBuffer` publish the per-chunk device
addresses the gather
kernel reads (`aclrtHostGetDevicePointer`) in a device tensor. That
tensor is created
while the sleep-mode weights pool is active but was neither a
`Parameter` nor a
registered buffer; level-2 sleep restores nothing but `named_buffers()`,
so the table
came back empty and the kernel dereferenced garbage (`SUSPECT REMOTE
ERROR`). The buffer
classes now register `{name}_ptrs` as a **non-persistent buffer**
themselves. `buffer_name`
and `module` are appended after the existing positional arguments, so
the original
`(shape, dtype, device)` / `(shape, dtype, device, group)` signatures
stay valid and the
tensor object (hence every address) is unchanged.

#### 4. Attention-sink weights must go through the loader —
`models/deepseek_v41/model.py`

`_load_model_weights` had a dedicated `if "sink" in name:` branch that
wrote
`param.data.copy_(...)` and `continue`d, bypassing the wrapped
`online_process_loader`.
A live update runs inside the layerwise reload, which only replays loads
made through
`weight_loader`, so the write was silently lost. It now routes through
`param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight.narrow(0, head_start,
heads_per_rank))`, the
same shape `deepseek_v4` already uses since #16958. `deepseek_v41` was
simply missed
there.

#### The E2E lane

Transformers has no `deepseek_v41`, so there is no meta model for the
shared
`FixedRandomWeightSource` to enumerate. `DeepseekV41WeightSource` (new,
`tests/e2e/common/rlhf/weight_transfer/deepseek_v41_weight_source.py`)
derives the payload
geometry from the published checkpoint's **own safetensors headers**
instead: an HTTP
Range request for the leading bytes gives `name -> dtype, shape` for a
shard without
downloading a single weight, cached under `DSV41_HEADER_CACHE` (and
bounded, so an
endpoint that ignores `Range` cannot pull a shard into memory).
`metadata` is a
`cached_property` and `iter_full()` forwards to `__iter__`, as current
vLLM requires.

`WeightUpdateModelCase` gains `weight_source_factory` (default
`FixedRandomWeightSource`), and `make_weight_source()` is now used by
both the NPU IPC and
HCCL entry points. The new case `deepseek-v4.1-flash-engram-cpu-offload`
lives in the
shared matrix (`tests/e2e/common/rlhf/weight_transfer/case.py`) with
`full_transfer_matrix=False`, i.e. selected on the unpacked NPU IPC lane
only, and is
driven by
`tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/rlhf/weight_transfer/ipc/test_deepseek_ipc.py`.

The case reads its model directory from `DSV41_MODEL_DIR` and **skips**
when it is unset
rather than pointing at a path that exists on one host. It keeps the
released shapes and
reduces only counts — experts 384 -> 8, Engram vocabulary 16M -> 40960,
MTP 3 -> 0 — which
turns the table into 986,214 x 256 bf16 (0.47 GiB, split over TP=2) and
makes a two-card
run possible. The reduction lives in the model directory's own
`config.json`, not in
`--hf-overrides`: `DeepseekV41Config` flattens the released
`text_config` onto the top
level, so a nested override replaces that sub-config and drops every
field it does not
restate (`num_attention_heads` among them), which `ModelConfig` then
rejects.

`npu_ipc.py` additionally returns the trainer's transient payload blocks
to the NPU
caching allocator **on every rank** after `send_weights()` and barriers
before rank 0
wakes the KV cache, so the co-located worker on the second chip cannot
find its memory
held by the trainer's cache.

Review follow-ups already addressed in this branch: `metadata` as a
`cached_property`,
`iter_full()` on the new source, the buffer/`module` argument order, and
the per-rank
`empty_cache()`/barrier above.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

**No.** No public API, CLI flag or config schema change, and `/sleep`
frees the same amount
of memory as before — the weights pool keeps its default `"weights"`
tag, and
`camem.py` and the transfer engines are untouched.

The new patch only changes what the layerwise reload materializes for
parameters that
explicitly carry a host range; everything else, including vLLM builds
without the reload
package, keeps upstream behaviour. The test-side additions are optional
environment knobs
(`DSV41_MODEL_DIR`, `DSV41_ENGRAM`, `DSV41_ENGRAM_CPU_OFFLOAD`,
`VLLM_RL_TEST_DEVICE_INDEX`,
`VLLM_RL_TEST_GPU_MEM_UTIL`) that all default to the previous behaviour.

### How was this patch tested?

**Lint / types (CI-equivalent).** `pre-commit` hooks (ruff 0.14 check +
format, codespell,
the repository's own import/logger/function-length hooks) pass on all 13
changed files, and
so does the mypy step the `pre-commit` job also runs (`mypy==1.11.1`,
`--follow-imports skip --check-untyped-defs`, Python 3.10 and 3.12, with
the vLLM source tree
on `PYTHONPATH` the way CI does it).

**Collection / unit.** `pytest tests/ut --collect-only` collects 16,503
tests with no import
errors. `tests/ut/models/test_engram.py` passes (102 tests), and the
engram + DeepSeek-V4.1
unit subset (`test_engram*.py`,
`worker/v2/test_deepseek_v41_engram_state.py`,
`patch/worker`, `test_deepseek_v41_{layer_plan,cache,registration}.py`)
passes: 452 tests.

**E2E on hardware.** Two NPUs, TP=2, against a 4-layer / 8-expert /
Engram-vocabulary-40960 bf16 checkpoint regenerated from the published
headers:


[Performance] Skip QSA CPU length sync for Ascend builder (#21758)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with MTP can skip the per-decode-step CPU
sequence-length synchronization when every metadata consumer accepts the
optimistic CPU upper bound and uses rejection-corrected lengths on
device.

The capability guard already allows the upstream
`Qwen4ExpQSAMetadataBuilder`, but the Ascend runtime instantiates
`AscendQSAMetadataBuilder`. Because the guard intentionally uses an
exact type allowlist, the Ascend builder misses the fast path and falls
back to `num_computed_tokens_event.synchronize()` on every decode step.
Profiling shows that this host synchronization breaks asynchronous
submission and creates bubbles between decode steps.

This PR:

- adds the audited `AscendQSAMetadataBuilder` to the exact allowlist for
`AscendQSABackend`;
- keeps conservative fallbacks for unknown builders/backends, DCP, PCP,
sparse KV offload, and real-time/interleaved multimodal inputs;
- updates the positive regression fixture to use the actual Ascend
builder;
- retains an explicit compatibility test for the upstream builder.

This is the `main` counterpart of #21589, which targets
`releases/v0.32.0rc`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It removes an unnecessary per-step host synchronization for the
supported Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Ascend QSA + MTP path, improving
pure-decode throughput and latency without changing the API or
configuration.

### How was this patch tested?

Latest-main validation:

- rebased onto vLLM Ascend `main` at `1f49be4c3`;
- `git diff --check`;
- `python -m compileall` for the changed implementation and test files;
- GitHub pre-commit: passed;

after rerun;

`tests/ut/models/test_qwen4_exp_spec_cpu_length_sync.py` — 22 passed;

[BugFix] Fix Qwen4Exp MTP position cache for long context (#21362)

## What this PR does

Fixes the long-context MTP position-cache mismatch for
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on the main branch while keeping the behavior change
scoped to the Qwen4Exp model implementation.

When the target model is started with `--max-model-len 1010000` and YaRN
overrides, the nested `Qwen4ExpMTP` draft config can still retain
`max_position_embeddings=262144`. During long-context graph replay this
undersizes the MTP rotary position cache and can lead to out-of-bounds
device access, Ascend error 507011, and `EngineDeadError`.

## Implementation

- Align the Qwen4Exp MTP draft position-cache capacity with the target
`max_model_len` before the upstream draft config and rotary embeddings
are constructed.
- Apply the adjustment only when the draft architecture contains
`Qwen4ExpMTP`.
- Grow only a draft using default RoPE; do not copy the target model's
YaRN parameters into the draft.
- Never shrink an already larger draft cache.
- Leave non-Qwen4Exp architectures and non-default draft RoPE
configurations unchanged.

The runtime change is contained in
`vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/mtp.py`. No shared worker or speculator
module is modified.

## Tests

Added Qwen4Exp-specific unit coverage for:

- long-context cache growth from 262144 to 1010000
- target YaRN parameters not being copied to the draft
- non-default draft RoPE being left unchanged
- larger draft caches not being shrunk
- other architectures being ignored
- alignment occurring before upstream draft-config construction

The same model-scoped logic passed 8 targeted unit tests and an A5
end-to-end regression on the release branch:

- 4/4 requests succeeded
- mean actual input: 1,008,004.25 tokens
- output: 1,024 tokens
- D-side occurrences of `507011`, `invalid GM`, or `EngineDead`: 0
- Proxy, P, and D endpoints remained healthy after the run

Release-branch counterpart: #21347.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is scoped to Qwen4Exp/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
- [x] Boundary and no-op paths are covered by unit tests.
- [x] The original long-context failure path has A5 regression evidence.
- [x] This is a user-visible stability fix and includes
`release_notes/fragments/21362.yaml`.
- [x] This is not a performance optimization and does not change
benchmark expectations.

[CI][Misc] Only cap build parallelism when CI passes MAX_JOBS=32 (#21977)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Follow-up to #21214, which baked `MAX_JOBS=32` / `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=32`
into the image `ENV` of all 8 Dockerfiles. That persisted the cap inside
the image and forced `setup.py`'s cmake `-j=32` on low-core machines,
which can OOM ordinary users building locally (e.g. 16Gi laptops).

This PR:
- Removes the persistent `ENV MAX_JOBS/CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` from all 8
Dockerfiles.
- Keeps bare `ARG MAX_JOBS` / `ARG CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` (no default value).
Docker automatically exports a `--build-arg` value into the `RUN`
environment, so no explicit `export` is needed: when CI passes
`MAX_JOBS=32`, builds are capped; when the ARG is unset, it is absent
from the environment and `setup.py`/`build.sh` fall back to `nproc`
parallelism.
- Passes `--build-arg MAX_JOBS=32 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=32` from the reusable
image build workflow (`.github/workflows/_schedule_image_build.yaml`),
so CI cluster builds are still capped while community/local builds are
unaffected.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Yes. The `MAX_JOBS`/`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` build args now default to unset
(nproc behavior); CI passes `32`. Users can still override via
`--build-arg MAX_JOBS=N` when building an image locally.

### How was this patch tested?
- `bash -n` syntax check on all modified RUN blocks in the 8
Dockerfiles.
- Docker build-time behavior verified: with `--build-arg MAX_JOBS=32`
the value appears in the RUN environment; without it the variable is
absent (so `os.getenv` returns `None` and `setup.py` uses `nproc`).

[Bugfix] Adapt batch-invariant initialization to torch-npu 2.10.0.post7 and CANN 9.2.0 (#21527)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Update batch-invariant initialization for the torch-npu 2.10.0.post7 and
CANN 9.2.0 stack.

Replace `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)` with
`torch_npu.npu.set_deterministic_level(3)` to explicitly request batch
consistency for supported NPU operators. The previous call enables
ordinary deterministic execution without selecting the batch-consistency
level.

Add a torch-npu version check to report an actionable error when the
configured version requirement is not met.

vLLM-ascend is currently compatible with torch_npu 2.10.0.post7 and CANN
9.2.0 [#20611](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20611) .

commits.message:
[CI] flip the required ci-gate check green in place on late owner approval (#22133)

A review used to spawn a separate pull_request_review verdict: when the
original pull_request run failed only because the CODEOWNERS approval
was missing at the time, the carry-forward logic could misread the
situation (a docs-only PR has select-tests legitimately skipped, which
shadowed the owner-resolved resolution), so the approval could never
turn anything green and the PR deadlocked with the comment asking for a
ready-precise label the PR does not need

Replace the review-event verdict machinery with a retrigger: on a
state-changing review from a CODEOWNERS owner of the changed files, the
new rerun-ci job re-runs the gate jobs inside the original pull_request
run, so the required E2E / ci-gate (pull_request) check itself updates
in place and the merge box reads a familiar single check name.

- APPROVED on a run whose only failures are codeowner-approval and its
ci-gate dependent: rerun-failed-jobs re-judges the gate with the current
reviews - green for docs-only PRs (which never need ready-precise) and
for already-green tests alike, red with a fresh comment otherwise.
- CHANGES_REQUESTED or dismissed on a green run: re-run the
codeowner-approval job (dependent ci-gate included, full run re-run as
fallback) so a veto re-arms the required check instead of being masked
by stale green.
- Reviews from non-owners and the PR author cannot change the verdict,
so they are filtered out via codeowner_gate's own parsing and matching
(single source of truth, fail-open on API errors); COMMENTED reviews,
bot reviews, code/test failures and already-green runs are no-ops;
conflicts with an in-flight retrigger are tolerated; a push that lands
while waiting skips the stale-head re-run.

[BugFix][EC Connector] Take memcache EC load shapes from the request (#20243)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

EC producers size each transfer before the item is encoded, and the size
depends on the encoder output width, which varies by model and modality.
Qwen3-Omni is the motivating case: its visual DeepStack output is 8192
wide (`out_hidden_size` 2048 x (1 + 3 DeepStack layers)) while its audio
output is 2048. Upstream vllm-project/vllm#57904 stopped inferring that
width from the HF config — which misses Qwen3-Omni, Granite4-Vision and
MOSS-Audio, none of which have a top-level `vision_config` — and now
measures it per modality at startup instead.

`ECMemcacheConnector` was not covered by that change. It still derived
one width from the model config and reinterpreted every loaded value
with it, so a value whose real width differed was either:

- **silently reshaped**, when its byte size happened to divide by the
assumed row stride, or
- **dropped**, logged as "not aligned with the encoder hidden
dimension", so the cache hit could not be used.

The reshaped case raises no error. On a real Qwen3-Omni service the
request still returns 200, but the model answers from a wrong embedding
(see the end-to-end result below).

This PR takes the layout from the request instead of the config:

- The scheduler records each `mm_hash`'s encoder embedding count
(`request.get_num_encoder_embeds(index)`), the same quantity upstream
uses to size Mooncake push specs. `mm_hashes_need_loads` becomes
`dict[str, int]` instead of `list[str]`.
- The worker derives each value's width from its byte size and that row
count, and reshapes with the derived width.
- Batching, offsets, capacity checks and the oversized-value path are
all computed in bytes, so values of different widths can share one
receive buffer.
- A key whose info is gone by the time the worker loads it (evicted
after the scheduler's lookup) is skipped instead of raising
`AttributeError` on `key_info.size()`. The caller already logs it as a
load miss.
- The config-derived width now only sizes the persistent receive buffer.
The worker connector is constructed before the producer measures widths,
so an underestimate there only routes more values through the existing
oversized path; it can no longer reshape data incorrectly.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Encoder-cache entries loaded from memcache are now restored with
their original shape for models whose encoder output width differs from
the LM embedding width. Previously those entries were either dropped or
reshaped into the wrong token count.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Unit tests

On this branch, then based on main `76ea9d24f`, with the release-tag
vLLM `v0.33.0`, CPU mode as in CI:

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python -m pytest \
  tests/ut/distributed/test_ec_memcache_connector.py -q
```

23 passed, 0 failed: 18 existing cases plus 5 new ones covering
mixed-width values sharing one buffer, a byte size that does not match
the request's row count, a key evicted before the load, the scheduler
recording row counts, and `start_load_caches` forwarding those counts.
Without the `None` check the evicted-key case fails with
`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size'`.

After a small readability change to `start_load_caches`, CI's `cpu-ut`
job ran the same 23 cases against both vLLM `v0.33.0` and the verified
vLLM main commit; all passed. The branch is now rebased on main
`6bfc5b33d` with no change to the patch.

#### End-to-end serving, real NPU and real memcache

Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Thinking served on an Ascend A3 host (2 chips, TP=2)
from the `nightly-main-a3` image, which ships vllm-ascend `3f1de8b04`
and vLLM `v0.33.0`, with `torch_npu` 2.10.0.post7, `memcache_hybrid`
1.3.0 and a private MetaService (`device_sdma`).

- **Before** is the image as shipped.
- **After** is the same container with only `ec_memcache_connector.py`
replaced by this PR's version. That file is unchanged between
`3f1de8b04` and the current base `6bfc5b33d`.

<details>
<summary>Launch command</summary>

```bash
vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Thinking \
  --served-model-name omni --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0,"audio":0}' \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECMemcacheConnector","ec_connector_module_path":"vllm_ascend.distributed.ec_transfer.ec_memcache_connector","ec_role":"ec_both","ec_connector_extra_config":{"recv_buffer_tokens":8192}}'
```

</details>

Each round sends three kinds of request, all at temperature 0:

1. Image A (1600x1600, upper half white, lower-left red, lower-right
blue; 2500 encoder embeddings) with the question "what colours are the
left and right of the lower half?". The encoder runs and the output is
saved to memcache.
2. 16 distinct 1024x1024 noise images, which evict A from the worker's
local encoder cache (budget 12544 tokens).
3. Image A again with the same question but a different sentence before
the image. A is now loaded from memcache.

The worker's own log shows how the loaded value was interpreted:

| | Worker log when loading image A |
| --- | --- |
| Before | `temporary_buffer_tokens=10000
persistent_capacity_tokens=8192` |
| After | `temporary_buffer_bytes=40960000
persistent_capacity_bytes=33554432` |

Before the fix the 2500-row value is treated as 10000 rows. After it,
40960000 bytes is exactly 2500 x 8192 x 2, and the scheduler metadata
carries `{mm_hash: 2500}`.

| | Answer to request 1 (encoded) | Answer to request 3 (loaded from
memcache) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before, 3 rounds | left red, right blue | **left blue, right red** in
2 rounds; no final answer within 400 tokens in 1 round |
| After, 2 rounds | left red, right blue | left red, right blue |

No error was logged in either arm and every request returned 200.

Two things worth knowing when reproducing:

- If request 3 repeats request 1 verbatim, the answer was not visibly
affected in my runs, presumably because prefix caching reuses the KV for
the image span. That is why step 3 changes the text before the image.
The same image in a different conversation, or on another node, is where
the bug surfaces.
- The log line above only appears for values that take the oversized
path, which before the fix and with `recv_buffer_tokens=8192` means more
than 2048 real rows. Smaller values are reshaped just the same but leave
no trace at INFO/WARNING level.

Scope of this run: one model, image modality only, eager mode, single
node, and base `3f1de8b04` rather than the current base.

#### Connector-level reproduction, real NPU and real memcache

On an Ascend A3 host, building the real `ECMemcacheConnector` through
its normal constructor against a private MetaService, with Qwen3-Omni
widths read from `config.json` and no model weights loaded:

| Value | Stored | Before this PR | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| image | (64, 8192) | **(256, 2048)**, `exact: false` | (64, 8192),
`exact: true` |
| audio | (50, 2048) | (50, 2048), `exact: true` | (50, 2048), `exact:
true` |

Audio was already correct because its width happens to equal the
config-derived width, which is why this only shows up on models with a
mismatched modality. This run predates the rebases of this branch and
has not been repeated.

#### Not run

Full `tests/ut`, end-to-end serving on the current base, multi-node
serving, and end-to-end audio or video.

> Note for anyone reproducing the connector-level run: `memcache_hybrid`
1.2.0 aborts at process exit with `double free or corruption (fasttop)`
while releasing its host DRAM segment. It is unrelated to this change —
a bare `DistributedObjectStore().init(...)` followed by process exit
reproduces it, with no EC connector involved — and it happens after all
data operations complete.

[Feature][Model] Support MiniMax M3.1 Flash DSpark on A2/A3/A5 (#20167)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Native MiniMax M3.1 Flash DSpark checkpoints use a five-layer draft with
Gemma norms, SwiGLUOAI, native tensor names and optional MXFP8 packing.
This PR integrates that draft into the standard Ascend plugin and
provides separate attention paths for compatible A2/A3 and A5
deployments.

- Discover and validate native `dspark/` configuration and BF16/MXFP8
tensors, preserve PTD/noise/mask aliases and independent draft
quantization, and reuse target embeddings/output head without rewriting
checkpoint files.

- On A2/A3, optionally select the ecosystem `flash_attn_npu_3` backend
for ordinary MiniMax target attention and paired DSpark/EAGLE3 drafts.
Preserve runtime causality/sliding windows, active request offsets, full
prefill lengths, KV write-before-read ordering, and graph-stable
scheduler buffers. Separate causal/noncausal graph storage and reject
metadata growth that would invalidate captured addresses.

- Keep A5 on its CANN attention path and sparse/indexer layers on their
dedicated backend. Keep the existing runner KV allocation policy: **no
changes to `attention/utils.py` and no new contiguity override**.

- Keep DSpark GQA FULL-graph Q lengths, KV lengths and block-table rows
at the same captured request extent. Remove an extra synthetic padding
row introduced by the generic target metadata builder before updating
draft FIA graph tasks. MLA metadata remains unchanged.

- Preserve fused sparse QKNorm/RoPE/cache preparation during DSpark
verification for supported BF16 and FP8 caches. Remove the blanket
DSpark exclusion while retaining the existing shape, dtype and layout
guards. The separate QK-norm/RoPE graph fusion pass remains disabled for
DSpark.

Native loading builds on [fork PR
#10](https://github.com/CXY-Katrina/vllm-ascend/pull/10). The A2/A3
addition ports the final ecosystem integration and guards from the
requested private PRs #9/#19, adapted to main's hardware-profile and
attention-transfer contracts. It does not reintroduce the superseded
standalone adapter, offline draft conversion or manual vLLM-core patch.
Unrelated release synchronization and deployment artifacts are excluded.

**Dependency: #19537 is still open.** The first two commits carry its
prerequisite (`bc7fed718` and `4d58a5049`, cherry-picked as `5803eab73`
and `8de2b4c3a`). The main-based diff therefore includes that dependency
until it lands; rebase to remove those prerequisite commits afterward.
The additional native Flash/A2/A3 support can be reviewed with `git diff
8de2b4c3a..HEAD`. Base main: `54b3258a6`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can load supported native Flash draft checkpoints through the
normal plugin. Existing external Qwen3 drafts retain their loading path.

A2/A3 automatic FA3 selection requires the optional `flash_attn_npu_3`
package (0.4.2.post2 scheduler API), FP16/BF16 queries, unquantized KV,
decoder attention, and PP/PCP/DCP size 1. Unsupported features or a
missing package retain the previous backend. This package differs from
the explicit training-consistency `flash_attn_npu_v3` backend. A5 does
not automatically select the ecosystem package even when installed;
native Flash CANN fast attention remains eager-only. Loader format
support is not a claim that every quantized checkpoint is supported on
every device generation.

Deployment documentation, patch removal guidance and
`release_notes/fragments/20167.yaml` are included. A compatible
target-model runtime is still required.

### How was this patch tested?

**252 CPU regression tests passed on the combined branch (181 existing +
71 A2/A3 integration cases).**

```bash

python -m pytest --noconftest \

  tests/ut/attention/test_minimax_ecosystem_fa3.py \

  tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_minimax_dspark_adapter.py \

  tests/ut/attention/test_minimax_dspark_integration.py \

  tests/ut/worker/test_spec_pp_cpu_counts.py -q --tb=short --maxfail=1

```

These run production helper/method bodies with CPU dependency stubs.
Coverage includes configuration/schema rejection, tensor/scale
preservation, native architecture validation, A2/A3/A5/310P selection
with/without the package, unsupported-feature fallbacks, scheduler API
arguments, padded requests, prefill bounds, causal graph-cache
isolation, stable storage across batch sizes, capacity overflow
rejection, KV update/transfer ordering, and DSpark versus non-DSpark
fusion registration. CPU stubs do not establish operator or hardware
correctness.

An A2/A3 numerical E2E test was added at
`tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_minimax_ecosystem_fa3.py` for
FP16/BF16, causal/noncausal attention, sliding windows, 7/8-token
queries, permuted pages and KV append against a CPU FP32 reference. The
existing A5 kernel E2E remains included. **Neither hardware suite was
run for this combined branch.** The user explicitly stopped the
evaluation services; no servers were restarted for this port.

The required `bash format.sh ci` was run. Ruff, formatting, spelling,
Markdown, C++ formatting, package/import, function-length and
symbolic-meta checks passed after formatting. The aggregate command
remains blocked by Windows `/bin/bash` resolution for the
Gitleaks/logger wrappers. The logger check passed when invoked directly
through Git Bash; Gitleaks was unavailable on PATH. ShellCheck and
actionlint (which may invoke it) were skipped as requested. Diff
whitespace validation allows the two existing CRLF files' line endings;
no unrelated newline conversion is included.

**Prior A5 evidence, before the A2/A3 port:** unchanged native loading
passed real-weight initialization, Quarot alignment, a request smoke
test and partial GPQA generation on an earlier integration stack
(`152a0322e`, Ascend `e8a6393dd`, PR20120, PR18426 removed, vLLM pin
below). An intermediate formal draft-token acceptance measurement was
about 23.35%; the requested 24% target was not established. All
comparisons were stopped before a full 198-question round completed, and
a separate AISBench reasoning-tag extraction issue was identified. No
final accuracy or speedup is claimed, and that run is not validation of
this latest-main/A2/A3 branch.

**Fused sparse preparation follow-up (2026-10-30):** Added BF16/FP8
dispatch and cache write-before-read regressions, plus six A5 numerical
comparisons against the unfused RMSNorm/RoPE/cache chain (8/128/192
tokens, independent KV/index page sizes and padded slots). A CPU-only
check executing the actual guard body covers 40 combinations: the
previous guard fails both supported DSpark cases; the corrected guard
passes all 40.

Hardware evidence was collected on Ascend main
`1eda0ddad8b67f791a1019741d254cc97f9617ad` + this PR + #18963 + the same
sparse-prepare fix, with vLLM
`544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`: 238 relevant unit tests, six
A5 numerical comparisons and eight cache graph replay tests passed. A
3-second TP8 eager decode capture contains 720 fused preparation kernels
followed by `MsaIndexScore` on each of eight ranks. This confirms
dispatch on that integration stack, not a graph-mode speedup or a
requirement for #18963. Partial non-streaming GPQA completed 68/198
requests (62 correct); the server then failed, so no full accuracy or
stability result is claimed. Services are stopped. The existing A2/A3
hardware-validation limitations still apply.

**DSpark graph padding follow-up (2026-10-30):** Real requests on A5
reproduced FIA error 561002: three KV lengths for a two-request captured
graph. Four regression cases fail before the fix; 167 related
DSpark/MLA/integration/MoE unit tests pass afterward. The corrected
integration (main `1eda0ddad`, matching vLLM above, this PR at
`8cb90663d`, and #20290) completed target FULL graph capture (5 sizes),
DSpark FULL graph capture (4 sizes), and a stable BS=16 decode profiling
window of 3.00006 seconds, with target and draft eager disabled. This is
graph-execution evidence, not a GPQA accuracy or end-to-end speedup
claim. Parsed kernel tables on all eight ranks each contain 3060 fused
sparse preparation kernels immediately followed by `MsaIndexScore`, and
2907 fused MoE `SwigluMxQuant` kernels. These counts verify dispatch on
the stated integration stack. The service and test containers are
stopped.

**Pending before merge:** #19537, standard vLLM-dependent suites, real
A2/A3/A5 checkpoint execution of this combined branch, numerical
kernel/graph replay tests, full accuracy and performance comparisons.
Historical private-branch results are not treated as validation of this
port. The PR remains draft.

[Ops][Feature] Support SWIGLUSTEP activation in W8A8 MXFP8 dynamic fused MoE (#21550)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The W8A8 MXFP8 dynamic fused MoE path previously ran SWIGLUSTEP
activation and MXFP8 quantization separately. This PR fuses them with
`npu_swiglu_mx_quant` using `swiglu_mode=3`, which matches SWIGLUSTEP's
post-SiLU clamp behavior.

The fused operator receives per-expert token counts through
`group_index`. The clamp limit defaults to `7.0` when the input value is
missing, `None`, or zero. The existing SwiGLU-OAI behavior is preserved.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, this is an internal quantization dispatch optimization for Ascend
NPU.

### How was this patch tested?

**Accuracy Evaluation**

GPQA accuracy evaluation was performed on Step 3.7 and Minimax M3.1
Flash to verify that the fused SWIGLUSTEP activation and MXFP8
quantization path introduces no accuracy regression.

| Model | Baseline | With this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Step 3.7 | 80.81% | 80.81% |
| Minimax M3.1 Flash | 87.88% | 87.88% |

No accuracy regression was observed on either model.

**Performance Evaluation**

Performance benchmarking was conducted to compare the original separate
SWIGLUSTEP activation and Dynamic MXFP8 quantization operators against
the fused `npu_swiglu_mx_quant` operator.

| Implementation | Average Latency |
| --- | ---: |
| Baseline: `_swiglustep_kernel` + `DynamicMxQuant` | 10.765 μs |
| With this PR: `npu_swiglu_mx_quant` | 6.030 μs |

The fused operator reduces average latency from 10.765 μs to 6.030 μs,
achieving a 43.98% latency reduction compared to the original separate
operators. These results demonstrate that fusing SWIGLUSTEP activation
and MXFP8 quantization provides a measurable performance benefit.

**Unit Tests**

Added unit coverage for activation dispatch, both scale algorithms,
count and cumulative group lists, operator arguments, and GMM2 scale
propagation in
`tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_swiglu_mx_quant.py`.

[BugFix][Spec Decode] Preserve DeepSeek V4 DSpark heads during weight loading (#17095)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #17094.

DeepSeek V4 DSpark maps both target and MTP-specific head/embed/HC
checkpoint keys to the same parameters. If `mtp.2.head.weight` arrives
before the target `head.weight`, the latter silently overwrites the
trained draft head. Unordered shard completion can therefore collapse
acceptance while requests still succeed.

This change gives MTP-specific parameters priority independently of
loading order:

- Track the five head/embed/HC destination names already loaded from
`mtp.*`.
- Skip subsequent target fallbacks for those parameters; allow later MTP
weights to replace earlier fallbacks.
- Preserve standalone and partial-MTP fallback behavior and the existing
rotation guards, without buffering checkpoint tensors.

The September 7 W8A8 checkpoint's `optional: {}` exposes the target
head/embed fallback path. This is a loader correctness fix, not a change
to checkpoint metadata, the forward path, or acceptance rules. The issue
contains a tiny checkpoint-free reproducer, the checkpoint comparison,
and the regression history (#13506).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: checkpoints containing dedicated MTP heads consistently use those
heads regardless of shard order, restoring speculative acceptance. There
are no new flags or API changes. Target weights remain fallbacks when
the corresponding MTP weights are absent.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added `tests/ut/model_executor/test_dspark_head_loading.py`: **262
passed**, covering explicit target-first/draft-first order, 128 seeded
shuffles, rotation present/absent, target-only fallback, and partial MTP
heads. The PR's complete model module was imported into the existing
Ascend test environment; only parallel-state accessors are mocked by the
tests.
- Negative control using the unmodified main model module: **243 failed,
19 passed**. The minimal issue reproducer produces `1.0 / 7.0` before
the fix and `7.0 / 7.0` after it.
- `bash format.sh ci`: passed (rerun after the shellcheck bootstrap
encountered a concurrent download/extraction error).
- Hardware validation of this same loader fix on the pinned nightly
stack: two 8 x 910B3 hosts, TP8 / K7, EP off/on; fresh model reloads
verified all 8 TP draft-head shards and all HC parameters against the
checkpoint, without runtime weight repair.
- Real-workload C1/C8: **512 formal requests passed** across two
consecutive warm 64-request batches per configuration/concurrency. C1
request-mean **pure decode TPOT**, excluding TTFT/prefill, recovered
from **48.70 to 12.20 ms (EP off)** and **49.16 to 12.50 ms (EP on)**.
This is recovery from corrupted draft weights, not a speedup over an
already-correct model.

Hardware measurements used Ascend `44f9bf53d` / vLLM `2cf0a6915` with
this loader fix. This PR is based on main `0003e1b75`; its
loader/remapper method ASTs are identical to the hardware-validated fix.
The complete latest-main serving stack has not been re-benchmarked.

To run the regression suite in a compatible development environment:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/ut/model_executor/test_dspark_head_loading.py
```

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with diagnosis, implementation,
tests, and this description. The commit includes AI attribution and DCO
sign-off.

[Misc][KV Transfer] Add concise heartbeat logs for MooncakeConnectorV2 (#21867)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The renewable leases introduced in #21425 report failures but provide
little visibility into normal heartbeat delivery and lease handling. Add
three concise log events for MooncakeConnectorV2:

- D emits one DEBUG `event=send` after each successful batch send, with
the producer endpoint and request count. No successful ACK logs or
request-ID lists are added.

- P emits one DEBUG `event=process` per heartbeat batch, counting
extended, unchanged, expired, and unknown request IDs. An unchanged
deadline is a valid outcome when the existing lease already lasts long
enough.

- P emits `event=lease_finish` once per completed lease: DEBUG for DONE,
ERROR for expiry with `expired_by_s`. Expiry logs retain the original
`Force freed expired Mooncake request ... after KV lease expired` prefix
for existing log searches, followed by structured fields including
`action=queued_for_release` to clarify the scheduler handoff.

Logging runs outside the lease state locks and uses deferred formatting.
The existing heartbeat failure warning now includes the exception type
and reason. No new configuration, periodic summaries, per-request
history, or wire-protocol changes are introduced.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Diagnostic logging only. Normal events require DEBUG logging; lease
expiry remains ERROR. Lease timing, renewal, ACK handling, and release
decisions are unchanged. No release-note fragment is included because
`release_notes/README.md` explicitly exempts internal logging changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added eight focused cases covering mixed/empty heartbeat outcomes,
exactly-once completion through DONE and both expiry paths, logging
outside state locks, and successful 512+1 batching after nonblocking
backpressure without ACK success logs.

- At head `4d7ad7169`, GitHub pre-commit and both CPU unit-test jobs
(pinned vLLM main and v0.33.0) passed. The CI gate still requires a
maintainer-selected test label; selected NPU CI jobs have not run.

- On Ascend A3, `python -m pytest -q
tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_pull_scheduler.py` passed: **137
passed**.

- Ran a 35-minute GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8 1P1D validation with a 131072-token
context limit, 128 concurrent background requests, 65536-token inputs,
and 32768-token generation budgets. All 128 first-wave requests reported
58880 cached prompt tokens (89.84%). The client resumed decode
recomputation using exact output token IDs; 81 background requests
completed the full 32768 tokens before validation ended, then
outstanding background requests were cancelled deliberately.

- Three 64K-input content probes submitted during the load retained
their P-side KV for **1615.46 / 1616.08 / 1615.68 seconds**, exceeding
the former 480-second threshold, and ended their leases through DONE.
All three returned the expected verification code, integer arithmetic
result, Chinese city name, and request identifier. The idle baseline
also passed.

- Observed 105 D send logs, 105 P processing logs, and 222 lease-finish
logs (including cleanup), totaling 83342 bytes. Heartbeats extended
leases 8204 times; normal-load expired/unknown counts were zero, with no
ACK success logs or server logging errors. A separate P-only request
with no D heartbeat expired after approximately 120 seconds and emitted
the preserved force-free ERROR prefix.

Runtime validation used an existing r93 openEuler container with this
exact PR source and the pinned vLLM source tree. Only heartbeat DEBUG
records plus ordinary INFO-and-higher records were enabled: unfiltered
shared-logger DEBUG exposed an unrelated existing MoE `%d`/`None`
formatting error. This validates heartbeat observability under load, not
globally enabling all DEBUG logs. No old-version inference A/B
comparison or controlled logging-overhead benchmark is claimed.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary and error-path coverage added.

- [x] Targeted remote unit tests, Linux pre-commit, and both CPU CI jobs
pass.

- [x] Real NPU pressure validation confirms renewal beyond 480 seconds,
content correctness, and the three log events.

- [ ] Maintainer-selected NPU CI gate completed (requires a
test-selection label).

- [ ] Performance impact measured (no controlled logging-on/off
comparison).
